structure: Part 3 of 3. Read the verbatim quote and preamble in full (lines 1-136), then sections (i) to (k), lines 496-706: claims 43-60. Section (i), claims 43-51, is plants changes in the same increment: Sam's rule (43), the orchestrator's mirror rules (44), row-by-row plants calls for journey-foundation, reference-lists, origin and arrival (45), consignment-parties (46), overview-and-review (47), manage-notifications (48), the 5 rows the mapping could not settle (49), the list rows inc-126 and inc-140 (50), and plants changes that need the plants backend being deferred (51). Section (j), claims 52-59, is the INS dashboard's summary information blocked (52), inc-127 going ahead (53), the new animals-dashboard theme (54), plants' list in it (55), inc-133 staying blocked and dependency changes (56), 'the overall dashboard' going to the set's own list (57), the germinal set's own list (58) and c-272 not needed (59). Section (k), claim 60, is the report grouping work as ready or blocked. Only claims 43 and 60 are Sam's own rulings; claims 44-59 are the orchestrator's application of his principles (points 7a, 7b, 7c, 8, 8a), so they are recorded as inferred and checked against the quote for points 7a, 7b, 8, 8a and 9. Gaps record what the quote leaves open there. No keeps.

claims.statement: Sam's point 9 does not say how ready rows are ordered among themselves, nor where a split row (built-now half ready, waiting half blocked) is shown in the report.

Sam's point 8 leaves open what the animals dashboard reframe must include beyond looking 'more like the animals dashboard on the prototype'; the row-by-row scope of animals-dashboard (claim 54) is the orchestrator's.
